rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Treasurer's Cash as of 6/30/2019`, PDF page 44 of the FY2019 annual town report (printed folio 42), a LANDSCAPE page, mediaBox 792x612 with /Rotate 270. READ, NOT RECOGNISED: pdfplumber returns 0 words on this page, and on every one of the 38 financial pages of this report. The page prints one label column and one money column, 37 account lines in alphabetical order from `Bank Hometown Investment` to `Unibank Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization`, then `Petty Cash / Certain Departments`, then `Total Treasurer Cash as of 06/30/2019  $15,084,021.00`. There is no column header to NAME (rule 13b.4), so the single money column is recorded as `balance`. ONE ASSERTION, TO THE CENT, NO TOLERANCE: the 37 account lines add to the printed total $15,084,021.00 exactly. WHY THIS PAGE WAS IN `extraction-blocked.csv` AND IS NOT A HARD PAGE: `extract_treasurers_cash.py` footed col0 to $11,763,248.59 against the printed $15,084,021.00, short by $3,320,772.41. That residual is EXACTLY the first four printed lines -- 521,202.60 + 1,848,802.86 + 56,512.43 + 894,254.52 = 3,320,772.41 -- and those four lines, with the page's title and heading, are absent from the committed OCR TSV because that TSV IS A CLIPPED RENDER. Measured, not assumed: re-OCR of this page with the current `scripts/ocr_pdf.swift` puts `Total Treasurer Cash` at y=0.14826 and `Belmont Savings Bank Investment` at y=0.74855, where the committed TSV puts the same two observations at y=0.1916 and y=0.9698 -- a factor of 792/612 = 1.2941 in y and 612/792 = 0.7727 in x, which is a 792x612 canvas carrying 612x792 of drawn content with the top 22.73% off the canvas. The committed TSV's topmost observation for this page is `Belmont Savings Bank Investment`; everything printed above it is gone. Rule 13c: the refusal was a statement about our render, not about the page.

The heading is `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2019`, printed on all four pages; the column header row reads `FISCAL YEAR` then `2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034 2035` on pp.49-50 (printed folios 47-48) and `2036 2037 2038 2039 2040 2041 2042 2043 2044 2045 2046 2047 TOTAL` on pp.51-52 (printed folios 49-50). The schedule is a 2x2: the SAME fifteen debt issues run down the side of all four pages, pp.49/51 carrying issues 1-13 and pp.50/52 issues 14-15 (whose headings are printed at the foot of pp.49/51 with no figures beside them), while pp.49/50 carry FY2020-FY2035 and pp.51/52 carry FY2036-FY2047 and the TOTAL column. Each issue prints `PRINCIPAL`, `INTEREST`, an `ADMIN FEE` row where it is a Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust borrowing, and a total row named for the issue (`TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST`, `TOTAL MUNICIPAL PURPOSE`, `TOTAL SCH GENERAL OBLIGATION`, `TOTAL MASS WATER POL TRUST-SEWER`, `TOTAL GOB MPL OF 2017`, `TOTAL DPW-ROADS GENERAL OBLIGATION`, `TOTAL MEADOW WOODS-SEWER GENERAL OBLIGATION`, `TOTAL MEADOW WOODS-WATER GENERAL OBLIGATION`). pp.50 and 52 then print `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST`, `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL & INTEREST`, `GRAND TOTAL MWPAT ADMIN FEES` and `TOTAL DEBT`, and the footnote `*MASS WATER POLLUTION ABATEMENT TRUST: PAYMENT AMOUNTS TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY EQUITY EARNINGS AND CONTRACT ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS`. TWO issue names are each printed TWICE -- `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE` and `MS-HS CONSTRUCTION` -- so four of the fifteen issues share a name with another, and `PRINCIPAL`/`INTEREST`/`ADMIN FEE` is printed under every one of the fifteen; so each issue is transcribed into its OWN file keyed by its PRINTED POSITION (01-15) and the fiscal year is the row key within it. Uniqueness was asserted directly rather than assumed. THIS FILE is issue 7 of 15 as printed, `MASS WATER POOL 14*`, with its total row printed as `TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST`. Its FY2020-FY2035 cells are on PDF page 49 and its FY2036-FY2047 cells and its printed TOTAL column are on PDF page 51. WHAT PROVES IT: this issue states two independent identities and this reading closes on both. (1) principal + interest + admin fee = the issue total, on each of its 10 year columns. (2) those 10 year columns sum to the TOTAL column the page prints beside them. Beyond this file, every figure in it also enters two further identities checked in `fy2019-p50-debt-grand-totals.csv` and `fy2019-p51-debt-issue-totals.csv`: the fifteen issues sum to the GRAND TOTAL row each page prints for that year, and the fifteen printed issue totals sum to the printed TOTAL corner. THE PAGE PRINTS DISPLAYED WHOLE DOLLARS OVER AMOUNTS THAT CARRY CENTS, so a printed total is the ROUNDED SUM and not the sum of the rounded parts. WHAT SAYS THAT RATHER THAN A MISREAD, and it is a contrast and not an assumption: the columns with no cents beneath them tie at ZERO. FIVE of the fifteen issues -- 03 and 06 MUNICIPAL PURPOSE, 08 MS-HS CONSTRUCTION (25 year columns), 12 GOB MPL OF 2017 and 13 DPW-ROADS -- close every row identity AND every column total EXACTLY, at zero tolerance. BOND PRINCIPAL ties exactly for thirteen of the fifteen issues and the fifteen printed issue principals sum to the printed corner `$46,568,549` EXACTLY; the printed MWPAT admin fees sum to the printed corner `$25,861` EXACTLY; and the corner itself closes at zero both ways -- 46,568,549 + 18,922,925 = 65,491,474 and 65,491,474 + 25,861 = 65,517,335. The two principal columns that do NOT tie are issues 02 and 07, Mass Water Pool trust borrowings whose principal amortises in cents. One wrong digit cannot leave that many independent sums perfect. NOTHING WAS WIDENED TO MAKE ANYTHING PASS (rule 14): every declared tolerance is stated with its derivation -- N displayed addends can differ from the rounded sum by at most N/2 + 0.5 -- and the observed maximum is given beside it. TOLERANCE FOR THIS FILE: $1. DERIVATION: 10 displayed addends, each rounded to the nearest dollar, so the sum of the parts can differ from the rounded sum by at most 10/2 + 0.5 = 5.5. The observed maximum on this issue is $1. THE TWO KNOWN DEFECTS OF THIS TABLE FAMILY WERE LOOKED FOR AND NEITHER IS PRESENT IN FY2019, read rather than assumed. (1) FY2011, FY2013 and FY2014 each print a `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row carrying a FY2024 principal of $418,704 with NO interest cell and NO total cell, which makes those schedules contradict themselves by $418,704. FY2019 prints the SAME balloon payment and prints it COMPLETE: p49 FY2024 reads PRINCIPAL $418,704, INTEREST $0, ADMIN FEE $314, TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST $419,018, and 418,704 + 0 + 314 = 419,018 exactly. Nothing on these pages omits a component. (2) FY2015 excludes two school-construction issues from every year column of its printed grand totals while including them in the TOTAL column. FY2019 does not: the fifteen issues sum to the printed GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL row in 25 of 28 years exactly and in the other three by $1, and to the printed corner within $2 on 213 displayed addends. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the schedule is a repayment SCHEDULE, not a ledger. It states what the town expects to pay and when; it is not a record of what was paid, and no cents are published anywhere on these four pages, so no figure here can be reconciled to the accounting system. Rule 11 applies to every line: these are gross debt service amounts and the footnote says in the town’s own words that the Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust payments are `TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY EQUITY EARNINGS AND CONTRACT ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS` -- so what the town actually raises against those lines is smaller than what is printed, by an amount this document does not state.
